title: Claude Fable 5 analyzed 30+ Phase 3 clinical trials and picked one biotech stock… it went up 22%. Coincidence?
author: Dh141437
selftext:
I wanted to share an experience and get some opinions from people who understand biotech / pharma investing and AI.

I chose a disease area that affects millions of people worldwide and asked Claude Fable 5 to analyze every company I could find with a Phase 3 clinical trial in that space.

This wasn’t a quick screening. Each Phase 3 study was a pdf of around 40+ pages, and there were over 30 companies. Claude compared the trial designs, primary and secondary endpoints, patient populations, inclusion/exclusion criteria, statistical considerations, previous Phase 2 data, mechanism of action, safety profile, competitive landscape, and what it thought were the probabilities of success.

It also analysed which companies would actually have a stock spike if the medicine would actually advance . 

At the end, it ranked the companies and strongly favored one stock over the others. Its reasoning was that this company’s trial design and existing evidence gave it the highest chance of producing positive Phase 3 results.  
I decided to invest based largely on that analysis.  
A few weeks later, the company announced positive Phase 3 results, and the stock jumped about 22% overnight .

Now I’m wondering… was this just luck, or are LLMs becoming genuinely useful at synthesizing huge amounts of scientific information that would take a human weeks to digest?

I’m **not** saying Claude predicted the future. Obviously, it didn’t know the trial results in advance. But it did analyze publicly available evidence and concluded that this trial had the highest probability of success before the results were released.

Has anyone else used AI this way for scientific papers, clinical trials, or biotech investing? Have you had similar experiences, or do you think this was simply a coincidence?
